newsitem.title: HONG KONG: I'm no lame duck, says Hong Kong Governor Patten.
newsitem.headline: I'm no lame duck, says Hong Kong Governor Patten.

text.p: The 28th and last British governor of Hong Kong took aim at those who dismissed him as a lame duck, insisting on Sunday he had his work cut out in the 296 remaining days of colonial rule.
"That familiar old pet, the lame duck, has come quacking out of the house of political cliches," Governor Chris Patten said in a Radio Hong Kong broadcast.
"Twenty-eighth and last governor means just that -- 28th and last," Patten said, but insisted that a very busy 10 months lies ahead in the countdown to the handover to China next June 30.
"We couldn't simply close down the government for the next 10 months and hope that it could be switched on again like a sports coupe, under winter wraps, next summer," he said.

The outgoing government has to protect the economy, see off "doomsters and any speculative sharks", and complete the task of bringing Hong Kong's laws in line with international covenants and the bill of rights, Patten said.
China has objected to Hong Kong's human rights bill and has threatened to water it down, but Patten declared no surrender.

"'Go quietly into the night' has never struck me as a very good motto or guide to leadership in a free society," Patten said. "So I shall continue to speak out, without, as they say, fear or favour, and I hope you will too."
